evaluation_protocol: Run the unchanged manifest against the lexical control and tree-sitter-kotlin 0.4.0 at one exact OpenClaw revision. Every arm uses a fresh database and the same 1024 source-token budget per task. A Kotlin candidate is accuracy-eligible only if relevant-file recall improves by at least one of 20 labeled files or line-anchor recall improves by at least five percentage points, with no task-family relevant-file regression. It must not regress existing product tests, exceed 10% cold-index or peak-RSS growth, exceed 5% database growth, or add more than 5 MiB to the release binary. Timing and memory thresholds require paired same-host runs and are interpreted as diagnostics on this ten-task development set, not universal performance claims. Accuracy eligibility does not waive the separate publication and supply-chain requirement: an unpublished grammar revision remains research-only.
reclassification_rule: The task labels and thresholds remain fixed for every arm. Any task, label, query, token budget, corpus revision, parser query, grammar revision, or threshold change creates a new schema/report version. This consumed development set must not later be described as blind or statistically powered evidence.
manifest_description: Prospective Kotlin structural-indexing evaluation over OpenClaw Android application and Wear shared owners. Prompts and labels were frozen from issue #366 and source inspection at the pinned revision before the Kotlin grammar candidate was integrated.

methodology.oracle_baseline: Full contents of fix-labeled relevant files, as if an agent chose every file perfectly and paid no discovery cost.
methodology.rg_discovery_baseline: Bounded, path-sorted ripgrep --json output for fixed-string queries derived from each public bug task.
methodology.scripted_baseline: One JSON envelope containing the ripgrep discovery output and oracle full-file reads.
methodology.source_tokens: Tokens in source content only; excludes paths, scores, reasons, receipts, and JSON syntax.
methodology.serialized_tokens: Tokens in the complete serialized JSON payload, including metadata and syntax.

corpora.name: openclaw-kotlin
corpora.prompt_provenance: Maintenance prompts were written from issue #366's named Android owners and public declarations at the pinned OpenClaw revision before the Kotlin grammar arm ran; no future patch or fix commit was consulted.
corpora.label_provenance: Relevant files and one-based line anchors were selected from declaration and regression-test ownership at the pinned OpenClaw revision before the Kotlin grammar arm ran.
external_limitations: The ten tasks are manually curated parser-development evidence, not a random or statistically powered sample.
Line anchors identify declaration and test neighborhoods; they do not prove that every returned line is sufficient to implement a correct patch.
Prompts name public or internal symbols to stress structural ownership and do not simulate an autonomous issue-triage trajectory.
The corpus contains both .kt and .kts files, while the retrieval tasks emphasize application maintenance; a separate bounded parse diagnostic covers both extensions.

tasks.prompt: Change resolveDefaultManualGatewayPort and composeGatewayManualUrl so TLS Tailnet hosts, trailing dots, and lookalike suffixes select the intended default port, and update regression tests.
Change ConnectionManager.resolveTlsParamsForEndpoint while preserving stored-pin precedence and rejecting discovery-advertised fingerprints as authoritative, with regression coverage.
Change InvokeCommandRegistry advertisedCommands SMS send and search availability independently while preserving capability advertisement semantics, and update registry tests.
Change InvokeDispatcher availabilityError and handleInvoke so location commands fail with the stable LOCATION_DISABLED contract when location is disabled, and update dispatcher tests.
Change mergeOptimisticMessages identity reconciliation so persisted history consumes matching optimistic turns without dropping repeated or newer messages, and update message identity tests.
Change PushToTalkTranscriptMerger overlap handling so final segments keep punctuation and duplicated trailing partials are omitted while distinct partials remain, and update merger tests.
Change TalkDirectiveParser first-line JSON alias handling while keeping case-insensitive keys, unknown-key reporting, and stripped speech text, and update parser tests.
Change parseWorkspaceListing and parseWorkspaceFile while preserving opaque entry paths, pagination metadata, text defaults, and base64 image payloads, with tests.
Change CanvasNavigationPolicy URL normalization so malformed, localhost, loopback, and encoded local web targets remain blocked while remote and bundled URLs remain allowed, and update policy tests.
Change WearRealtimeAudioFraming read and write validation so frame boundaries round-trip and oversized payloads are rejected before allocation, and update Wear shared tests.

limitations: The oracle baseline assumes perfect file selection and reads whole files rather than exact decisive ranges.
The scripted ripgrep baseline uses fixed queries supplied by the manifest and is not an autonomous agent trajectory.
No model executes an edit, so this runner does not measure pass rate, prewalk handoff quality, or end-to-end task cost.
Cold indexing and warm latency depend on host hardware and filesystem cache state.
Validation prompts and labels were frozen from open issue reports and pinned source inspection, then used during retrieval tuning; this is not blind holdout evidence.
The validation tasks are retrieval development evidence, not a statistically powered product claim.
